name: Nemuel
overview: Nemuel was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, identified specifically as the son of Eliab and grandson of Pallu. He is noted in Scripture as a progenitor of the Nemuelites, a clan mentioned in the Book of Numbers. His lineage places him within the genealogical records important to Israel's tribal organization.
namesAndTitles: The name Nemuel appears only once in the biblical text, and no specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to it in the given references. It functions as a proper name identifying this individual within his tribal context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Nemuel as the son of Eliab, who himself is a son of Pallu. No other familial relationships are explicitly documented beyond this direct paternal line.
scriptureSignificance: Nemuel's significance lies in his role as an ancestor of the Nemuelite clan within the tribe of Reuben, demonstrating the detailed genealogical records maintained in the wilderness census. This lineage highlights the faithfulness of God's preservation of the tribes of Israel through successive generations as they journeyed toward the Promised Land.
